title: AMD's Lisa Su courts Korean AI chipmakers as it takes on Nvidia
key_facts: Su met Second Vice Science Minister Ryu Je-myung and executives of 13 Korean AI companies in Seoul.
Plan: pair AMD CPUs and GPUs with Korean neural processing units for AI inference, for global markets.
Demonstration projects in Korea would test the systems to build a blueprint for overseas deployment.
Participants explored joining AMD's open-source ROCm software, which competes with Nvidia's CUDA.
AMD reaffirmed an AI Center for Excellence in Korea by year-end, hiring hundreds of researchers; location not yet chosen.
Talks followed a July cooperation agreement between AMD and the science ministry.
Su was expected to meet Samsung vice chairman Jun Young-hyun.
quote_evidence: Su discussed pairing AMD's CPUs and GPUs with Korean neural processing units designed for AI inference.
The partnerships could expand AMD's inference offerings and give Korean chipmakers a route to global customers, broadening AMD's challenge to Nvidia in AI computing.
AMD will fund hardware for the center, whose location has yet to be selected, according to the ministry.
why_it_matters_hint: Korean AI chip makers may reach global customers through AMD systems.
